text:
matt: ran the PP bubble profiling sweep on the 8xA100 cluster this morning. microbatch=4, sequence=2048, model=redwood-bert-13B-fp16. bubble still ~40% of step time. attaching top-line traces from perf-bot below.

perf-bot: auto-profile results (summary):
```
step_time: 182.4ms
compute: 108.6ms (59.6%)
all_reduce_total: 31.2ms (17.1%)
comm_wait (idle due to bubble): 42.6ms (23.4%)
KV-cache lookup overhead: 6.1ms
```

matt: interesting bit: the all_reduce is mostly overlapping with compute on TP ranks 2-3 but PP stage boundaries show big gaps (1F1B schedule not fully filling). kernel selector switched to the new fused-attn kernel at commit a3f4c2 last week — perf regression window?

sara: did you try microbatch=8? that usually reduces bubble by increasing granularity for 1F1B. also what's the batching heuristic (dynamic vs fixed)?

matt: tried microbatch=8 earlier, step_time dropped to 161ms but latency tail increased. dynamic batching was on with max_batch=16. interestingly, when we forced fixed microbatch the KV-cache hit rate improved (less small-prefix variance) so cache overhead dropped ~2ms.

kevin: can we overlap NCCL all_reduce with computation better? i.e., launch async nccl ops earlier and use CUDA streams to overlap. also check NCCL_P2P_LEVEL / NCCL_ASYNC_PROGRESS settings. on recent kernels these flags moved perf.

jana: noted similar in my run: enabling cudaMemcpyAsync + separate comm stream reduced comm_wait by ~9ms but introduced extra memory pressure on the input pipeline. we should measure peak mem and OOM risk. also try switching to 1F1B tuned schedule with warmup=2 (see config snippet).

matt: config I used:
```
pp: { stages: 4, microbatches: 4, schedule: "1F1B", warmup: 1 }
batching: { mode: "dynamic", max_batch: 16 }
kernel_selector: { policy: "auto", allow_fused_attn: true }
```

jana: try this tuned variant:
```
pp: { stages: 4, microbatches: 8, schedule: "1F1B", warmup: 2 }
batching: { mode: "fixed", max_batch: 8 }
comm: { async_nccl: true, stream_affinity: "compute+comm" }
```

matt: will run both today. quick note: flamegraph from perf-bot shows kernel-switch overhead at the boundary where fused-attn falls back to generic attention for long-seq chunks — that fallback triggers extra memcpy + recompile-looking cost (~4-6ms).

perf-bot: posted flamegraph link: https://perf.redwood/fg/1768881234/ (flamegraph + nccl timeline). :eyeglasses:

sara: if fused-attn fallback is the culprit we can force old kernel on those sequence lengths to compare. please log the kernel selection traces (enable SEL_TRACE=1).

kevin: also watch all-reduce algorithm: ring vs tree matters at TP sizes > 2. ring has lower memory but higher latency; hierarchical trees can reduce latency if we have NVLink pods. run NCCL tests with -b and -t.

matt: quick preliminary: forcing fused-attn=false (revert selector) with microbatch=4 increases compute by 8ms but reduces bubble by 12ms -> net win. so the new fused path might be causing serialization at stage boundaries. suspicious.

jana: file a perf regression issue referencing commit a3f4c2, include perf-bot traces and the kernel selection logs. tag runtime/pp and eng-ml.

matt: filing issue now. minimal repro: 4 stages PP, seq=2048, microbatches=4, model=redwood-bert-13B, fused-attn toggle. attaching logs in the issue.

sara: great. after issue we should run the 1F1B warmup=2 + async_nccl config across the fleet testbed and measure median+p99. if stable we can roll as an opt-in runtime flag.

kevin: cc @infra-team for possible NCCL env defaults change.

matt: thanks all — will post results by EOD. :thumbsup:
